title: Min Stack
summary: Design a stack class that can also report its smallest value. `push(val)` puts `val` on top, `pop()` removes the most recently pushed value, `top()` returns that value without removing it, and `getMin()` returns the smallest value still in the stack. Every one of the four operations must run in O(1) time.

examples.input: push(3), push(5), push(2), getMin(), pop(), getMin(), top()
examples.explanation: Popping 2 removes the minimum, so the next getMin() falls back to 3, the smallest value left.

examples.input: push(4), push(1), push(1), pop(), getMin(), pop(), getMin()
examples.explanation: 1 was pushed twice, so after one pop it is still the minimum; after the second pop, the minimum is 4 again.

constraints: pop, top and getMin are only called when the stack holds at least one value

approaches.twist: Push each value together with the smallest value at or below it, so the top always holds the current minimum.
Keep a plain stack and scan every value in it for the smallest one each time getMin is called.
approaches.note: Works, but getMin reads every value on the stack, so it takes O(n) time. The target is O(1) per operation.

approaches.twist: Push each value onto both the stack and a min-heap, and lazily discard heap entries that were already popped from the stack.
approaches.note: Works, but every heap push and pop takes O(log n) time. The target is O(1) per operation.

signals.meaning: Last in, first out. A Python list is already a stack: append pushes and pop removes the newest value, both in O(1).

signals.phrase: smallest value still in the stack
signals.meaning: The minimum only changes on a push or a pop. Let each entry remember the smallest value at or below it; after a pop, the new top already knows the minimum of what is left.
Scanning for the minimum costs O(n) per getMin. To answer at once, have the answer ready from the pushes instead of searching when asked.

constraintReading: Up to 3·10⁴ calls. If getMin scanned the stack, 1.5·10⁴ pushes followed by 1.5·10⁴ getMin calls would read about 2·10⁸ values: O(n) per call. The O(1) target for every operation rules that out, so the minimum must be ready before anyone asks; one extra number per entry keeps the space at O(n).
